evidence_proposals.excerpt_or_summary: Turchin and Joslyn present a new control level as a metasystem transition, and propose a future integration compatible with individual freedom; these are their philosophical and normative claims.

evidence_proposals.locator: Opening paragraphs; Background of the theory
evidence_proposals.excerpt_or_summary: The project names MSTT its particular philosophy, encompassing knowledge, metaphysics, evolutionary history, forecasts, and ethics, rather than only the transition mechanism.
S-prime includes S-type subsystems and an additional mechanism controlling their behaviour and production. The scale can be one, with no replication, if a control level emerges.
Heylighen proposes combining variation and selection with cybernetic organisation and control, and criticises observer recursion in second-order cybernetics. This is his programme statement.

evidence_proposals.locator: Evolutionary Ethics; Human Development; Competition Between Levels
evidence_proposals.excerpt_or_summary: Heylighen and Turchin say values cannot be derived from natural facts, then develop survival and continuing evolution as commitments, and acknowledge conflicts between levels.
Turchin defines transition through new control and, in his social example, treats integration as necessary but insufficient. His case is an interpretation rather than proof of social benefit.

evidence_proposals.locator: Printed pp. 10-12, A constructive epistemology; An evolutionary ethics (1-based PDF pages)
evidence_proposals.excerpt_or_summary: Heylighen describes models as constructed for purposes and environmentally selected; he says values cannot be deduced from natural facts while adopting evolutionary continuation as an ethical purpose.

profiles.title: Evolutionary cybernetics
profiles.canonical_definition: A programme investigating how organisation and control emerge and develop through evolutionary processes; the account here follows Principia Cybernetica.
profiles.summary: Heylighen proposes investigating how control and goal-directed organisation emerge and develop through evolution. His page also advances a broad interdisciplinary philosophy. Its critical account of second-order cybernetics is his interpretation, not a settled history of the field.
profiles.why_it_matters: Distinguish a research programme and its proposed mechanisms from established consensus.
key_distinctions: The page proposes that variation and selection underlie evolutionary phenomena; this broad claim requires argument and domain-specific evidence.
A descriptive selection process does not, by itself, decide whose survival or welfare should count.

profiles.title: Metasystem transition
profiles.canonical_definition: In the Principia account, emergence of a new level of control over a system or systems.
profiles.summary: The project describes S-prime as containing S-type subsystems and an additional control mechanism. Its scale is the number integrated; the minimum is one, when a new control level appears without replication. Turchin treats integration as necessary but insufficient in his social example.
profiles.why_it_matters: Ask what is controlled, what new controlling mechanism appears, and what evidence demonstrates it.
key_distinctions: Aggregation or integration alone does not establish a new control level.
The definition does not establish that an observed transition is beneficial, inevitable, or just.

profiles.title: Metasystem transition theory
profiles.canonical_definition: The Principia editors’ particular cybernetic philosophy, organised around the emergence of new levels of control.
profiles.summary: MSTT extends beyond the definition of a transition: its project overview includes epistemology, metaphysics, evolutionary history, predictions, and ethics. It proposes that models are constructed by subjects or groups and selected by their environment.
profiles.why_it_matters: Identify which part is a definition, an empirical historical interpretation, a future forecast, or a value commitment.
key_distinctions: An example offered as a transition needs independent examination of its claimed control mechanism.
Evolutionary continuation and survival are the authors’ values, not observer-neutral measures of welfare.
